turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, mister. Washington, come on back. Before we get going, can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Darnell Washington. February 9th, 1968.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect thank you. How was the drive -in? I heard the parking garage was full again this morning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, it was. I circled three times and ended up on the street two blocks down.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Sorry about that, so this is your blood pressure follow -up. How have things been since we saw you in July?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Pretty good, mostly. I've been checking it at home, like you said, and it's still kind of high, usually like 145, 150 on the top number.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, that's helpful, and what are you taking for it right now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The lisinopril, 10 milligrams in the morning. Wait, no,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: it's 20.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: You bumped it up last time, remember, I've got the new bottle in the car.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Right, 20 milligrams once a day. Are you taking it every day?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every day. I keep it next to the coffee maker, so I don't forget.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good trick, and you're still on the adorvastatin for your cholesterol.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, forty milligrams at night. That one I never miss.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Great. Any headaches, chest pain, or trouble catching your breath.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, none of that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any dizziness when you stand up or swelling in your ankles.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any cough since you've been on the lisinopril. Some people get a dry, tickly cough with it. Nah, no cough. How about salt? Last time you said you eat out a lot for lunch.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Um, yeah, still work lunches. Lots of deli sandwiches and chips. I know, I know.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And alcohols.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A couple beers on the weekend, that's about it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, and you mentioned your dad before, right?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, my father had a stroke at 62.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's kind of why my wife Lorraine stays on me about all this. that makes sense she's looking out for you all right your blood pressure today is 152 over 94 and when I rechecked it after you sat quietly for five minutes it was 148 over 92 pulse is 72 weight is 214 pounds that's up three pounds from July yeah that's the Halloween candy starting early I guess let me take a listen heart sounds regular no murmurs lungs are clear and no swelling in your legs. I also have your labs from last week. Your potassium was 4 .4 and your kidney function was normal, creator 9 -0 .9. And your LDL cholesterol was 88.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is that good?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The cholesterol is right where we want it. And the kidneys and potassium look fine, which means we have room to go up on the lisinopril.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So here's what I'm thinking. Your blood pressure is still above our goal of under 130 over 80, even on the 20 milligrams. I'd like to increase the listen -up rule to 40 milligrams once a day. Until you run out, you can take two of your 20s together in the morning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two of the 20s, got it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep the Adorvastatin the same, 40 milligrams at night. I'd also like you to cut back on salt, aim for less than 2000 milligrams a day. The deli meat and chips are big ones.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I can try packing lunch. Lorraine will be thrilled.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That would help a lot. Since we're raising the dose, I want to repeat potassium and kidney check in about two weeks. You can go to our lab on Brookfield Avenue, no appointment needed.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm off on the 19th. Does that work?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The 19th is perfect. Keep checking at home and bring your log next time. If you get readings over 180 on the top or a severe headache, chest pain or weakness on one side, call us or go to the emergency room.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Will do.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And I'll see you back in six weeks. Is your cell still 5550163?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yep, same number.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Great, any other questions for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I think that's it. Thanks, Doc.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Take care, Darnell. Good luck with the parking on the way out.
